With the consent of both the parties matter is heard finally.

2 The appellant/company has preferred this appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short MV Act) being aggrieved by the impugned award dated 9.5.2017 passed by MACT Ratlam in claim case No. 45/2015 whereby an amount of Rs. 57,16,474/- has been awarded to the claimants towards compensation.

3. Fact of the case in brief are that on 24.8.2014 at about 4.15 pm when deceased Chandrashekhar alongwith his wife was coming from Pawagadh by Tempo Trax bearing registration No.
G.J.-17/W-3815, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver Kalyansingh, the vehicle capsized due to which Chandrashekhar sustained grievous injuries and he has been died.
Accordingly offence has been registered.

4 The claimants/respondents has filed the claim petition under section 166 of MV Act before the below tribunal claiming compensation of Rs. 40 lakhs with interest on account of death of husband/father.
The appellant No. 1 (before the below tribunal) is widow of deceased and other appellants are daughters of deceased.
The respondent no. 5 herein is the owner of the offending vehicle and the vehicle was insured with appellant no. 1 /company.
The age of deceased was 54 years at the time of incident and he was working in MP Electricity Division and was earning Rs. 70 thousand per month alongwith DA and other allowances.

5 The appellant/respondent no. 2 by filing written statement opposed the averments made in the claim petition by stating that at the time of incident, driver Kalyan singh was not having any valid and effective license for carrying the said vehicle.
The said vehicle was driven against the terms and condition of insurance policy, therefore, the company was not responsible, hence claim be dismissed.

6 The claims tribunal after framing issues and recording the evidence available on record has allowed the claim petition by awarding amount of Rs. 57,16,474/- to the claimants as compensation with interest @ 6% p.a.
Being aggrieved by the finding given by claims tribunal, the appellant/insurance company has preferred this appeal.
7 Learned counsel for appellant contended that at the time of incident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving license.

He was driving the transport vehicle for which the endorsement /transport is necessary but at the time of incident he was possessing LMV license and not authorized for driving the vehicle in question, therefore, the terms and condition of insurance policy has been violated.
All these aspects have been ignored by the below tribunal while passing the award.
Hence it is prayed that impugned award be set aside and appellant be exonerated from the liability of payment of claim amount.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for respondents/claimants contended that the impugned award passed by the below tribunal is just and proper and based on cogent evidence available on record which does not deserve for any interference.
9 I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

10 From perusal of the impugned award it appears that below tribunal has discussed in paras 10 to 13 of the award that driver of offending vehicle was possessing the driving license to drive the LMV but the vehicle was not used as transport vehicle at the time of incident.
Therefore, respondent no. 2 has failed to prove that terms and conditions of insurance police has been violated.

11 In the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, AIR 2017 SC 3668,
Apex Court has held that if licence holder is possessing driving licence to drive light motor vehicle (LMV), then he can drive tractor attached to trolley and there is no need to obtain separate endorsement and it is not breach of police.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, AIR 2017 SC 3668
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case of Jagdish Kumar Sud Vs.
United
India Insurance Company Limited

and another, AIR 2018 SC 2906, Apex Court has held that if the driver is having licence of driving LMV, he is entitled to drive the light commercial/transport vehicle of which weight is not exceeded 7500 kgs.

12 In the present case, it is not disputed that at the time of the accident driver of the offending vehicle was driving LMV vehicle and perusal of the record of the tribunal it is found that weight of the offending is below 7500 kgs.
so as per the verdict of the Apex Court mentioned above, there is no need of separate endorsement for driving the transport vehicle whose weight is below 7500 kgs.

13 In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court this court is of the considered opinion that at the time of incident the driver was having effective and valid driving license, therefore, there is no breach of any insurance policy and the insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the claimants.
The first liability to pay the compensation is upon the insurance company.
The insurance company is firstly liable to pay the compensation jointly/severely.
The below tribunal has discussed all these facts and legal aspects while passing the award.
Therefore, the impugned award passed by the below tribunal is just and proper.
14 In the result, this appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE BDJ Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Smt. Meena on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99176140/
